 whereby the Award dated 20.05.1992, passed by the Reference Court,
 granting compensation at the rate of Rs.400/- per sq. yard to the  appellant for the acquisition of his plot measuring 566 sq. yards,
 has been set aside and the matter has b  Reference Court for a fresh decision in accordance with law.
 3. The controversy has arisen out of acquisition of 61.801  acres of land by the respondent  Authority, which included a plot  measuring 566 sq. yards owned by the appellant.  Reference under Section 18 of the Act, which was answered in his  favour vide an Award dated 20.05.1992, granting compensation at the  2 rate of Rs.400/- per sq. yard.
Earlier, the High Court set aside the aforesaid Award on 20.04.2004.
The appellant then approached this Court and vide Order dated 24.04.2006 passed in C.A.No.2217 of 2006 and connected matters, this Court remanded the matter to the High Court for fresh adjudication.
Pursuant thereto, the High Court has passed the impugned order dated 18.01.2010, again remanding the case to the Reference Court.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and carefully perused the material placed on record.

5. According to learned counsel for the respondent  Authority, the controversy regarding rate of compensation has been settled by the High Court during the pendency of this appeal and that judgment of the High Court has been upheld by this Court as well.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the appellant states that keeping in view the prominent location of his acquired plot, its potentiality for commercial or residential utilization etc., the appellant is entitled to a higher rate of compensation.

sentences.text: Since the High Court has not gone into the merits of the case, we deem it appropriate to set aside the impugned order dated 18.01.2010 and remit the case to the High Court for adjudication of First Appeal No.603 of 1992 on merits.
8. It goes without saying that we have not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case and the parties shall be at liberty to raise their respective pleas before the High Court.

9. Keeping in view the fact that this is an old matter where the acquisition commenced way back in the year 1988, the High Court  3 is requested to decide the First Appeal preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt/production of a copy of this order.
10.
The appeal stands disposed of in the above terms.
